result.title: LLM Detoxification via Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling
result.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate toxic content, motivating effective test-time detoxification. Existing representation steering methods often rely on static or coarse interventions and provide imprecise guidance because they inadequately model transitions between toxic and non-toxic generations. We propose Transition-Aware Reward-Guided Representation Sampling (TARGRS), a test-time framework that learns reward guidance over toxicity transitions in latent representation space. During exploration, progressive steering along the toxicity direction constructs trajectories from non-toxic to toxic states. Toxicity scores along these trajectories turn sparse annotations into dense, listwise supervision for a transition-aware token-level reward model. During inference, TARGRS uses this model to guide coarse-to-fine sampling along the opposite, non-toxic direction: coarse sampling identifies the intervention needed to reach non-toxic regions, and refinement selects a detoxified representation with minimal perturbation. Experiments on 10 LLMs across RealToxicityPrompts, BOLD, and AttaQ show that TARGRS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, reducing toxicity by up to 69.38% on RealToxicityPrompts. TARGRS runs nearly as fast as the original LLM while preserving its core capabilities with minimal impact. By intervening in the language decoder space, TARGRS also extends to Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), reducing toxicity by up to 64.23% across 3 representative LVLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TARGRS 测试时去毒框架：沿毒性方向渐进引导构造从无毒到有毒的表示轨迹，用轨迹上的毒性分数训练 token 级奖励模型，推理时反向沿无毒方向做由粗到细的表示采样并取最小扰动解。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在 latent 表示空间中用奖励模型引导由粗到细采样与扰动最小化」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的筛选、干预与验证提供可核查的方法线索，但任务本身为安全去毒而非视觉推理。
